title: Choose the visual world for the SmartHR portal
question: The roll assigned The Marked Answer Script. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Marked Answer Script
options.lineage: Indian board-exam answer booklets and the examiner's marks grid on the cover
options.thesis: Every candidate is examined like an answer script: a mark per requirement, the reason in the margin, the total boxed.
options.viewport: Teal job rail on the left; the ranked list as rows whose right side is a marks grid, one boxed cell per requirement (tick, half, cross), total boxed in examiner red.
options.risk: Red ink can read as 'error'; it must stay reserved for marks and totals, never for failure states.

raised.raise: Every candidate shows its distance to the next band, e.g. '−6 to Strong fit', like a stop-delta.
The candidate being reviewed stays highlighted in the list while you move through the queue with J/K.
Each job tab in the rail carries a bar whose length is its applicant count.
Verdict is fill, not colour: solid cell met, hatched cell partial, empty cell not found.

options.label: The Lab Report
options.lineage: Indian diagnostic lab reports: test, observed value, reference range, flag
options.thesis: Each requirement reads like a test result: observed evidence, the reference it was checked against, and a flag.
options.viewport: Navy letterhead header with job and rubric version; the candidate view is a report table: requirement, observed quote, verdict flag, weight.
options.risk: Familiar and safe; also the clinical, form-like direction many runs land on, so it can feel cold over long sessions.

options.label: Gate Board Shortlist
options.lineage: airport departure boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: The shortlist is a live board: candidates rerank in place when thresholds change, and a moved row stays lit until noticed.
materials: segmented pass for the candidate view
options.viewport: Ranked board as the whole first view; candidate opens as a segmented 'pass' with fit, band and must-haves as stubs.
options.case: Strong on clarity (rescoring visibly reranks rows); weaker on identification than an exam script.
options.risk: Airport theming can turn into costume if the board look outruns the data.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Pack the whole shortlist, rubric and evidence onto one screen so a recruiter never pages.
options.viewport: A mosaic: job modules, rubric module, ranked table and evidence preview tiled edge to edge in one view.
options.case: Holds clarity for fast scanning; loses identification with Indian HR and tires the eye over long sessions.
options.risk: Tiny type and heavy density can breach comfortable reading for an all-day tool.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Overlapping translucent sheets with hatch density as data.
options.case: Loses both axes: recruiters do not know darkrooms, and hatching obscures verdicts.
options.kept: Distance to the next band shown as a number, like a stop-delta.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Every screen as the next decision point.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere fatigues an all-day tool.
options.case: Loses both axes against the exam script for this audience.
options.kept: The candidate you are on stays highlighted as you move through the queue.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Sections as coloured tab boards under acetate leaves.
options.viewport: Stepped tab rail down the edge.
options.case: Loses both axes; the tab rail is its only transferable discipline.
options.kept: Job tabs sized by applicant count.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Shape and fill as the whole vocabulary.
options.case: Loses both axes; its fill encoding is the part worth keeping.
options.kept: Verdicts encoded by fill (solid, hatched, empty), never by colour alone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern applicant-tracking dashboard, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, job header, candidate cards with a score pill each.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every ATS by design.
